Vivek Singh Thakur, J. (Oral)
This appeal has been listed today, for considering objection raised by the Registry regarding the maintainability of the appeal as the compensation amount awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT), in a Claim Petition preferred under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act (MV Act) is less than Rs.1,00,000/-.
2.

The very basis of raising objection by the Registry is the provision of Section 173(2) of MV Act which reads as under:-
"(2) No appeal shall lie against any award of a Claims Tribunal if the amount in dispute in the appeal is less than [one lakh] rupees"
Whether reporters of the local papers may be allowed to see the judgment?
3. The present appeal has been preferred by the claimant for enhancement of compensation amount as the MACT has awarded only Rs.40,000/- against the claim preferred by the claimant for compensation of Rs.3,00,000/-.

sentences.text:
4. As per Registry, for quantum of amount of compensation awarded by the MACT, i.e. Rs.40,000/-
only, the bar for filing and maintaining an appeal imposed under Section 173(2) comes into play and thus the appeal is not maintainable.
5. Provisions of aforesaid sub-Section(2) of Section 173 provides that no appeal shall lie "against any award" of Claims Tribunal if the "amount in dispute in the appeal" is less than Rs.1,00,000/-.
6. I am of the considered opinion, that the view taken by the Registry is erroneous for the reasons assigned hereinafter.

7. "Amount in dispute in the appeal" does not mean the amount awarded by the MACT in the claim petition, particularly when claimant has preferred claim petition for amount higher than Rs.1,00,000/- and for awarding lesser compensation by MACT he prefers an appeal claiming compensation for an amount more than Rs.1,00,000/-,
8.
"Amount in dispute in the appeal" means the amount being claimed by the appellant and disputed by the respondents.
In present appeal, amount of Rs.40,000/- is not an accepted or claimed amount.
The 'amount in dispute' is claim of Rs.3,00,000/-.
9. Appeal against award of Rs.40,000/- shall not be maintainable against the award in present case by owner/driver/Insurance Company etc.

In case the appeal is preferred by the person or the Institution upon whom liability to pay Rs.40,000/- has been fastened, the amount in dispute would be less than Rs.1,00,000/- because, in such a situation, amount in dispute would be the amount awarded by the MACT which in present case is Rs.40,000/-.

10. But in case of claimant, who has already filed a petition for compensation amounting to into Rs.3,00,000/-, the 'amount in dispute' would be Rs.3,00,000/- but not Rs.40,000/- at any stretch of imagination.

11. There is a difference between an "appeal preferred for enhancement of compensation" and an "appeal preferred against the liability fastened" by the MACT upon a person or the Insurance Company".
12.

Being a beneficial legislation, enacted for awarding just and fair compensation to the victims of the motor accidents, it can never be intention of the legislature to debar a claimant from filing appeal by the claimant either for enhancement of the compensation or against the dismissal of his claim petition filed by him for compensation amount more than Rs.1,00,000/-.

13. In case, amount claimed by the claimant in the original claim petition is less than Rs.1,00,000/-
then bar created in sub Section (2) of Section 173 shall be applicable for the reason that in such eventuality 'amount in dispute' between the parties would be less than Rs.1,00,000/-.
14. In case interpretation of Registry is accepted, then there shall be no appeal available to a claimant whose claim petition has been dismissed by the MACT.
